Factors affecting parents' choice of schools for Grade 1 learners (ERIC)

claims.text: Perceived quality gaps in public schooling trigger migration to a limited functional sub-system, because parents evaluate schools by academic outcomes rather than proximity or default assignment.
Financial and informational scarcity converts zoning policy into a forced constraint, because affordability and local access override all other school attributes.
objections: Is this school in my zone, or will I be forced to accept it?
Can I afford the transport and fees, or is proximity my only real filter?

claims.text: Higher parental education transforms school choice into an active marketplace search, because informed criteria like learner-teacher ratios and teacher passion become the filters for decision-making.
objections: How do I find out about teacher quality and the curriculum before I enrol?

claims.text: Perceived threats to safety and discipline turn schools into risk environments, because parental vigilance and willingness to exit become the primary safeguards for the child.
objections: What do other parents say about discipline and safety here?

claims.text: When traditional norms lose relevance, choice becomes preference-driven, because parents formulate new ideal-school aspirations and make trade-offs in pursuit of perceived quality.

confidence: Multi-source qualitative synthesis drawing on author-interpretation and participant voice; single-province fieldwork with small samples — mechanisms are robust within the studied contexts, but magnitudes and national prevalence are unknown.
